title: NITI Aayog releases report on India’s Services Sector: Insights on Regulatory Regime in Professional Services
body_text:
Shri Ashok Kumar Lahiri, Vice Chairman, NITI Aayog, launched the third report under the Services Thematic Series at the forum of the High-Powered ‘Education to Employment and Enterprise’ Standing Committee, in the presence of Smt. Nidhi Chhibber, CEO, NITI Aayog, and Dr. Saurabh Garg, Secretary, MOSPI, on 10th August 2026. The launch was attended by senior officers from the Ministries/Departments, State Governments, Industry Associations, and Experts/Academia, who are members of the High-Powered Committee.
The report, “ India’s Services Sector: Insights on Regulatory Regime in Professional Services ”, presents a unique factual assessment of India’s regulatory framework in professional services and benchmarks it against select foreign jurisdictions. Drawing on extensive stakeholder consultations, it also identifies key challenges and outlines a way forward to strengthen the sector and unlock the full potential of India’s professional workforce.
Professional services is a key sub-sector in the services economy, accounting for nearly a quarter of India’s total services exports. As high-value, knowledge-intensive activities, they enable efficient delivery of downstream services, support job creation and remittance inflows, and form the backbone of the services value chain. Understanding the regulatory ecosystem governing these services is therefore critical to unlocking further growth.
The report adopts a balanced approach and provides sector-specific insights, alongside a four-pronged strategy to enhance the efficiency and output of professional services: harnessing emerging trends to transform professional services; elevate professional services within the services value chain; adoption of best practices in professional services, and continuous professional development for professionals.
As India approaches its demographic peak, professional services oﬀer significant opportunities for high-skilled employment, entrepreneurship and innovation. A well-designed regulatory ecosystem can further strengthen service exports, cross-border mobility of professionals and the ease of doing business.
The report provides an indicative pathway for future policy dialogue and deeper examination of the regulatory foundations of professional services. As India advances towards Viksit Bharat @2047, such eﬀorts will be integral to building a globally competitive, inclusive and future-ready services sector.
Read the full report: https://www.niti.gov.in/sites/default/files/2026-08/India-Services-Sector-Insights-on-Regulatory-Regime-in-Professional-Services.pdf

enrichment.summary: On 10 August 2026, NITI Aayog Vice Chairman Ashok Kumar Lahiri launched the third report in the Services Thematic Series, titled 'India's Services Sector: Insights on Regulatory Regime in Professional Services'. The report benchmarks India's regulatory framework for professional services against select foreign jurisdictions and proposes a four-pronged strategy—leveraging emerging trends, elevating professional services in the value chain, adopting best practices, and continuous professional development—to strengthen the sector. It notes professional services account for nearly a quarter of India's total services exports.
enrichment.context:
Professional services (such as legal, accounting, architecture, engineering and consultancy) are high-value, knowledge-intensive activities that support downstream service delivery, job creation, and remittance inflows. India's services sector is a major contributor to GDP and exports, and as the country approaches its 'demographic peak', policymakers see high-skilled professional services as a key avenue for employment generation, entrepreneurship, and global competitiveness. Regulatory barriers—such as restrictive licensing, limited cross-border recognition of qualifications, and fragmented state-level rules—have historically constrained the growth and export potential of these services in India compared to peer economies.

This report is part of NITI Aayog's broader Services Thematic Series, which appears aimed at generating an evidence base for future services-sector reforms under the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047. It follows India's efforts to negotiate mutual recognition agreements and ease cross-border mobility for professionals under various trade and services agreements. The report itself is a diagnostic and advisory document rather than a binding policy change, intended to inform future policy dialogue among ministries, states, and industry on modernizing professional services regulation.

prelims_questions.question: With reference to India's services sector, consider the following statements: 1. Professional services account for nearly a quarter of India's total services exports. 2. The 'Services Thematic Series' report on professional services was released by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states professional services account for nearly a quarter of India's total services exports; the report was released by NITI Aayog, not the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

prelims_questions.question: The report 'India's Services Sector: Insights on Regulatory Regime in Professional Services' was released under which committee/forum mentioned in the release?
options: High-Powered 'Education to Employment and Enterprise' Standing Committee
prelims_questions.explanation: The report was launched at the forum of the High-Powered 'Education to Employment and Enterprise' Standing Committee, as stated in the release.

mains_questions.question: Professional services are described as a critical link in India's services value chain. Discuss the regulatory challenges facing professional services in India and suggest reforms to enhance their global competitiveness.

India's demographic profile presents both an opportunity and a challenge for high-skilled service sector employment. Examine how regulatory reform in professional services can help harness India's demographic dividend.
mains_questions.gs_paper: GS Paper 2 - Governance and Social Justice

study_notes.reason: The release primarily flags a diagnostic NITI Aayog report and its four-pronged strategic recommendations for reforming professional services regulation, which is analytically useful for GS3/GS2 answers on services exports and regulatory reform; the only sharply testable fact is the 25% export-share figure and the existence of the Services Thematic Series, so factual depth is thin.

prelims.point: This report is the third in NITI Aayog's 'Services Thematic Series', launched by Vice Chairman Ashok Kumar Lahiri on 10 August 2026.
prelims.why_important: UPSC often tests which institution/series a report belongs to and its sequence number.

prelims.point: Professional services (legal, accounting, architecture, engineering, consultancy) account for nearly a quarter of India's total services exports.
prelims.why_important: A precise export-share statistic is a classic prelims fact that could appear in a statement-based question on India's services trade.

mains.point: Regulatory barriers such as restrictive licensing, limited cross-border recognition of qualifications, and fragmented state-level rules have historically constrained the growth and export potential of India's professional services compared to peer economies.
mains.analytical_use: Useful for 'Discuss the regulatory bottlenecks facing India's professional services sector and suggest measures to enhance its export competitiveness' type questions.

mains.point: The report's four-pronged strategy—leveraging emerging trends, elevating professional services in the value chain, adopting global best practices, and ensuring continuous professional development—offers a policy framework for sectoral reform.
mains.analytical_use: Can be cited as a way-forward framework in answers on strengthening India's services exports or professional-services competitiveness.

mains.point: As India approaches its 'demographic peak', professional services are positioned as a key avenue for high-skilled employment, entrepreneurship, and innovation, linking regulatory reform to the broader employment-generation challenge.
mains.analytical_use: Supports answers on harnessing India's demographic dividend through high-value service-sector jobs and the role of regulatory ease in enabling this.

low_priority.point: List of dignitaries and committee members present at the launch event (CEO NITI Aayog, MOSPI Secretary, industry associations, academia).
